"Flyover Fintech has become an annual tradition where public and private sector leaders from across the country gather in Lincoln at Nebraska Innovation Campus to talk about the future of fintech," said Congressman Flood. "Whether it's digital assets, housing, AI, and more, Flyover Fintech has something to offer for everyone. Space is limited, so I encourage you to check out the website and get registered today." events.title: Wildlife Photography by John Ritchey
events.description: Wildlife Photography is a collection of images captured across Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and Nebraska that highlights the beauty and behavior of wildlife throughout the American West. Through patience and observation, John Ritchey documents animal behavior in natural environments, capturing moments that reveal how animals communicate, hunt, protect their young, and respond to their surroundings. Long hours in remote areas require both awareness and respect for wildlife, while also providing opportunities to study movement, interaction, and instinct. John Ritchey is a professional wildlife photographer residing in Lincoln. He began pursuing photography as a full-time passion following his retirement in 2009 after serving 24 years as an Integrated Avionics Systems Mechanic for the Nebraska Air National Guard. From 2007-2008, he also served as a house photographer for the Qwest Center. View his gallery: https://api.flickr.com/people/ritcheyjj/. For purchase inquiries, he can be reached at (402) 610-5267 or jritc65610@yahoo.com. This exhibit is free and open to the public daily from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: 26th Annual Nebraska Grazing Conference
events.description: Make plans now to attend the 2026 Nebraska Grazing Conference at the Younes Conference Center in Kearney, NE on August 4-5. The theme of the conference will be Celebrating Grazing on Nebraska's Grasslands as part the 2026 International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists. The conference will begin on afternoon of Tuesday, August 4. Tradeshow talks on the 4th will focus on Virtual Fence Technologies for better grazing management followed by a celebration of the 2026 International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists. On Wednesday, August 5, a full day of speakers will be focused on regenerative grazing management, grazing on croplands, small ruminant grazing, conservation grazing practices, and grazing stockmanship. Keynote speaker's include Gail Fuller (https://farmersfootprint.us/gail-fuller) who will speak on regenerative grazing management practices. Dr. Tom Noffsinger will highlight the importance of stockmanship in grazing management. Hother speakers will present on Carbon Credit markets and opportunities on grazing lands. High school and university students are encouraged to attend. Student registration fees are waived for those registering online before July 15. https://grassland.unl.edu/nebraska-grazing-conference-registration/ Celebrating Grazing on Nebraska's GrasslandsStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Ag Robotics Conversation Series: Marble Technologies with Chafik Barbar
events.description: Join us for a conversation with Chafik Barbar, CEO of Marble Technologies, as part of our Ag Robotics Conversation Series. Marble Technologies tackles some of the toughest challenges in the food supply chain. Based in Lincoln, Nebraska and Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company uses AI, robotics, and process engineering to add resiliency to the agrifood supply chain. Starting with meat processing, Marble Technologies automates tasks to address industry-wide labor shortages while advancing worker safety, sustainability, and efficiency. In this session, Chafik will share how Marble Technologies is building and deploying robotics in real processing environments, what it takes to bring automation into one of agriculture's most demanding sectors, and where the company sees the biggest opportunities ahead. This webinar is designed for industry leaders and startups working in or around ag robotics, automation, and the food supply chain. events.title: Applied Data Cleaning Workshop
events.description: Summary Do you have data that is not ready for analysis? Are you unsure what all you need to do with "dirty" data? In this workshop, we will go through what data cleaning means, what you should know in preparation for data cleaning, and best practices before working with a provided dataset in Excel to fix common issues found in "dirty" data. We will also discuss common ways to modify the structure of variables to meet analytic needs. If time allows, we will talk about managing identifiers and adding data points. This workshop is a combination of interactive lecture and hands-on work in Excel with a tabular dataset. Focus is on general data principles, with some specific information related to human subjects, quantitative, and qualitative data. Registration is required, and space is limited. Registration link: https://research.unl.edu/events/event_nuramp.php?EMSEventUUID=a0f3d533-1a8d-46cf-bd40-5f7870976640 Learning objectives * Increased awareness of different data issues and how to address them * Ability to manipulate data for greater analytic utility Possible bonuses * Greater familiarity with Excel * Tips and tricks that make your adventures with data easier Prerequisites Participants are expected to have some familiarity with Excel, such as the ability to use formulas and make tables. Knowledge of pivot tables is a bonus, but will also be demonstrated. Optional micro-credential credit This workshop counts 5 credits towards the optional Research Data Life Cycle Micro-credential. Sign in for credit will be at end of workshop. Learn more about the Micro-credential here: https://researchdata.unl.edu/foundations/rdlc-micro-credential/ Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: First Friday at Great Plains Art Museum
events.description: The Great Plains Art Museum is open late Aug. 7, 5-7 p.m. with three exhibitions, light refreshments, and an insect and butterfly origami activity in the lower-level education studio. On view: "Jennifer Angus: Like a Moth to the Flame" August 7-December 19, 2026 | First-Floor Galleries Jennifer Angus creates site-specific, immersive art installations that utilize dead and dried insect specimens to create environments that are often described as otherworldly, magical, and sometimes uncomfortable. Over time, Angus's work has evolved to consider issues related to the environment and the important role insects play within it. "Like a Moth to the Flame" explores the Great Plains region, an ecosystem home to the Sandhill crane migration, American bison, mountain lions, foxes, badgers, and countless other mammals. Less visible, though no less essential, are the nearly 30,000 insect species that inhabit this landscape, most living unseen beneath leaves, within soil, and among grasses. This exhibition invites visitors into that hidden world, asking them to imagine themselves insect-sized, dwarfed by the sculptural works around them. Within this immersive environment, the extraordinary adaptability of insects becomes visible, revealing how these small creatures sustain the intricate balance of an interconnected ecosystem. The opening reception for "Like a Moth to the Flame" will take place at the Great Plains Art Museum on Aug. 19, 6-8 p.m. with artist Jennifer Angus. Angus is a professor of Design Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Described by "Art Daily" as "one of the top contemporary installation artists in the country," Angus has exhibited widely across the United States, being one of nine artists selected for the landmark exhibition "WONDER" at the Smithsonian American Art Museum's Renwick Gallery in 2015. This exhibition at the Great Plains Art Museum is presented in collaboration with CAREMI-the Community for Arthropod Research, Education, and Materials Innovation-a transdisciplinary initiative at UNL that brings together researchers, engineers, artists, educators, students, and community members to harness the diversity and resilience of arthropods as sources of knowledge, inspiration, and innovation. This exhibition is supported by the Nebraska Arts Council and the Nebraska Cultural Endowment. "Moving with the Hydrocommons" August 7-December 19, 2026 | Mezzanine Gallery A commons is a shared resource that is vital to collective life and the relations such a resource instantiates. The "hydrocommons" extends this idea to water. "Moving with the Hydrocommons" is an exploration of water and bodies within, around, and beyond the Great Plains. Following the inquiry, "What does water teach?" and drawing from collected vignettes, personal reflections, and contextual research, a screendance was choreographed as an exploration of water across bodies-social, historical, geographic, sensorial. A companion zine shares the contributed narratives, movement and sensory scores, and other watery notations for moving with the hydrocommons. "Moving with the Hydrocommons" is Mac Kelsey's project as the Center for Great Plains Studies' 2025-26 Student Storyteller in Residence. Kelsey is a teacher, artist, researcher, and PhD candidate in Educational Studies (Teaching, Learning, and Teacher Education) at UNL. She focuses on developing curricula and pedagogies for technology/media studies, cultural theory, and somatic practices in education. The Student Storyteller in Residence program is funded by the Michael Farrell Fund for Student Storytelling, administered through the University of Nebraska Foundation. "With a Little Help from Our Friends: New Perspectives on the Collection" March 6-August 8, 2026 | Lower-level Gallery Organized in honor of the Center for Great Plains Studies' 50th anniversary in 2026, this exhibition highlights the important interdisciplinary focus of the Center and its core intellectual community, the Great Plains Fellows. The Fellows as a group are scholars and community members who are concerned with the past, present, and future of the Great Plains, and they support the Center and its mission in myriad ways. For this exhibition, 20 Fellows representing diverse disciplines and all four University of Nebraska campuses were invited to select an artwork from the Great Plains Art Museum's permanent collection and respond to it in any way they chose, whether that's examining the work through their scholarly lens or through their own lived experiences.New exhibitionsStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Native American Film Series
events.location: Mary Riepma Ross Media Arts Center-Van Brunt Visitors Center Room:Ross Theater (123)
events.description: Now in it's third year, the Native American Film Series at The Ross features free monthly screenings showcasing Native American films and television programs from the Vision Maker Media public broadcasting archives. Presented by The Ross Media Arts Center, Vision Maker Media, and Friends of The Ross. Unless otherwise noted, screenings in this series will take place on the second Monday of each month and are admission free and open to the public. Tickets available at the Ross box office (online ticketing not available for free screenings). Showing in June: AANIKOOBIJIGAN [ANCESTOR / GREAT-GRANDPARENT / GREAT-GRANDCHILD] // In the sterile archives of museums our ancestor's remains struggle to find their way home. The film follows the eleven indigenous repatriation specialists that make up MACPRA (Michigan Anishinaabek Cultural Preservation & Repatriation Alliance). Through an essayistic approach the film takes a critical look at the reasoning that justified unearthing and collecting them in the first place, and presents vrit portraits of the courageous individuals doing the hard and emotionally draining work of fighting for their return. The June 8 screening will be followed by a discussion with Zack Khalil (Director/Producer/Cinematographer), Jacque Clark (Producer/Additional Cinematographer/Sound Recordist), and Samuli Haavisto (Cinematographer). Moderated by Shirley Sneve (ICT Newscast Senior Producer).Ross EventStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: South Central Ag Lab Field Day
events.description: The University of Nebraska South Central Agricultural Laboratory (SCAL) Field Day is on Tuesday, August 11, from 8:30 a.m. to 1:45 p.m. at the SCAL research farm. Through interactive topics, growers will gain insights into practical applications they can consider incorporating into their own operations. Attendees can tailor their schedule by selecting from various presentations and interactive demonstrations. Lunch will be provided, and attendees can earn Continuing Education Units (CCA credits). Preregistration is appreciated by Sunday, Aug. 9, to assist with lunch planning. Visit go.unl.edu/scalfieldday to register and for program details. Registration, coffee, rolls and visits with sponsor tables begin at 8:30 a.m. with the welcome and opening remarks by sponsors kicking off at 8:45 a.m. Dr. Salvador Ramirez II is the keynote speaker during lunch. Ramirez is an Agroecosystem Management Research Associate with USDA-ARS in Lincoln, NE and a UNL Doctor of Plant Health Graduate - 2019. He will discuss how soil organic carbon (SOC) in irrigated continuous corn is shaped by how tillage, residue management, and cover crops interact. Stacking conservation practices like no-till, full stover retention, and cover crops enhances SOC compared to conventional systems. Ramirez will provide a first-hand account of what the USDA-ARS is learning in biomass studies and how the practices could look in grower fields. Timely topics include: * Evaluating the Critical Time of Hairy Vetch Termination for Control of Palmer Amaranth in Sorghum and Popcorn * Overlapping Residual Herbicide Program for Control of Palmer Amaranth in Soybean * Updates on Insect Pests in Eastern Nebraska * What's Below the Surface? Matching Corn Hybrids, Seeding Rates, and Nitrogen for Better Performance * Irrigation Management Strategies * Soybean Disease Management for South Central Nebraska * Corn Disease Update: Why 2026 is So Different from Last Year? The SCAL Research Farm is located at 851 Hwy. 6 near Harvard, NE. Directions: 13 miles east of Hastings on Hwy. 6 or 4.5 miles west of the intersection of Hwy. 14 and Hwy. 6 north of Clay Center. Field day GPS coordinates: 40.575256, -98.137824. For more information, call (402) or email shachtel1@unl.edu. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Soybean Management Field Day/TAPS Field Day
events.description: For over 25 years, growers have benefited from the latest advancements in soybean production, management and marketing at Soybean Management Field Days. This year marks the second year that the Soybean Testing Ag Performance Solutions (TAPS) competition highlights are included in the field days, including lessons from last year's contest and progress this season. The field days provide an opportunity to learn about cutting-edge soybean management, production practices and technologies, while networking with fellow farmers and industry experts. The three-fold focus of the field days is to provide practical information, foster dialogue and showcase collaborative efforts: * Learn about best practices and strategies to apply in your fields. * Engage in productive discussions on issues ranging from local to global. * Explore Nebraska Soybean Board (NSB) initiatives in research, marketing and education. "Our goal is to give growers real value they can take home and use," said Andy Chvatal, NSB executive director. "By highlighting programs like TAPS, we're helping producers evaluate new ideas and learn directly from the results. In addition to TAPS, the field days also focus on timely topics that matter most to growers, including disease management, market updates and practical production strategies." Throughout the four-day event, attendees will be able to participate in two different formats, one occurring in the evening and the other during the day. The evening meetings, held Aug. 11-13, will feature presentations on locally relevant topics and engage participants in interactive discussions. To conclude the week on Aug. 14, a field day starting mid-morning will highlight the Soybean TAPS contest with interactive discussions and a plot tour. Soybean Management Field Days is free to attend thanks to support from NSB. To help with a meal count, please pre-register two days in advance of each field day at go.unl.edu/soydays or by calling 402-624-8030. Tuesday-Thursday - (evening) 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. CST (5:30 registration) * August 11 - North Platte, NE * August 12 - Central City, NE * August 13 - Crete, NE Friday - TAPS field day (morning/afternoon) 10:30 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. CST (9:30 registration * August 14 - University of Nebraska ENREEC near Mead, NE Attendees will also have the chance to hear from MEG Corp about soy biodiesel and connect with representatives from NSB and Nebraska Soybean Association at each location. Registration and information about the field days, including maps to the event sites can be found at go.unl.edu/soydays, or contact NSB at (402) 441-3240 or Nebraska Extension at (402) 624-8030. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Part 107 Remote Pilot Exam Prep Course
events.description: This 1-day (8-hour) course prepares students to pass the FAA Part 107 Aeronautical Knowledge Exam required to receive a remote pilot certificate (aka drone license). Covers aviation topics such as regulations, airspace, radio communication, weather, aircraft performance, and other basic aviation concepts necessary to pass the exam. events.title: Soybean Management Field Day/TAPS Field Day
events.description: For over 25 years, growers have benefited from the latest advancements in soybean production, management and marketing at Soybean Management Field Days. This year marks the second year that the Soybean Testing Ag Performance Solutions (TAPS) competition highlights are included in the field days, including lessons from last year's contest and progress this season. The field days provide an opportunity to learn about cutting-edge soybean management, production practices and technologies, while networking with fellow farmers and industry experts. The three-fold focus of the field days is to provide practical information, foster dialogue and showcase collaborative efforts: * Learn about best practices and strategies to apply in your fields. * Engage in productive discussions on issues ranging from local to global. * Explore Nebraska Soybean Board (NSB) initiatives in research, marketing and education. "Our goal is to give growers real value they can take home and use," said Andy Chvatal, NSB executive director. "By highlighting programs like TAPS, we're helping producers evaluate new ideas and learn directly from the results. In addition to TAPS, the field days also focus on timely topics that matter most to growers, including disease management, market updates and practical production strategies." Throughout the four-day event, attendees will be able to participate in two different formats, one occurring in the evening and the other during the day. The evening meetings, held Aug. 11-13, will feature presentations on locally relevant topics and engage participants in interactive discussions. To conclude the week on Aug. 14, a field day starting mid-morning will highlight the Soybean TAPS contest with interactive discussions and a plot tour. Soybean Management Field Days is free to attend thanks to support from NSB. To help with a meal count, please pre-register two days in advance of each field day at go.unl.edu/soydays or by calling 402-624-8030. Tuesday-Thursday - (evening) 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. CST (5:30 registration) * August 11 - North Platte, NE * August 12 - Central City, NE * August 13 - Crete, NE Friday - TAPS field day (morning/afternoon) 10:30 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. CST (9:30 registration * August 14 - University of Nebraska ENREEC near Mead, NE Attendees will also have the chance to hear from MEG Corp about soy biodiesel and connect with representatives from NSB and Nebraska Soybean Association at each location. Registration and information about the field days, including maps to the event sites can be found at go.unl.edu/soydays, or contact NSB at (402) 441-3240 or Nebraska Extension at (402) 624-8030. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: 2026 Soybean Field Day - ENREEC
events.description: August 14th - Mead, NE - Eastern Nebraska Research, Extension & Education Center - Google map: https://go.unl.edu/smfd4 * Topics - Join us Friday morning to hear from a variety of speakers. We will lead off with insights learned from three years of the Soybean TAPS competition, then Garrett Ruskamp of Pioneer Farmer, will walk through the five common and costly mistakes that quietly drain farms and practical steps to correct them. You'll also receive an overview of current disease and insect pressure in soybeans. At lunch, you'll hear from MEG Corp about biodiesel use as well as your local Nebraska Soybean Board and Nebraska Soybean Association representatives. In the afternoon, you'll have the opportunity to tour the Soybean TAPS competition plots and visit with researchers out in the field about what they are seeing. The Nebraska Soybean Board and Nebraska Extension would like to invite you to attend one of the four Soybean Management Field Days being held August 11-14th.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: 2026 Nebraska Small Business Conference
events.description: The annual Nebraska Small Business Conference will be held in Grand Island, Omaha, and Lexington in August 2026. This bilingual event (English and Spanish) supports both new and experienced entrepreneurs. Centered on the theme "Small Business, Smart Future," the conference will explore how technology and artificial intelligence are shaping the future of small businesses. Attendees will hear from experts and entrepreneurs, gain practical tools, and learn strategies to grow in today's digital world. Participants will also have opportunities to network and visit exhibitors offering resources for business success. Topics include marketing, social media trends, technology, and access to funding. The conference is organized by Rural Prosperity Nebraska's Small Business Program in collaboration with SCORE, providing guidance and training to help entrepreneurs succeed. events.title: Wildlife Photography by John Ritchey
events.description: Wildlife Photography is a collection of images captured across Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and Nebraska that highlights the beauty and behavior of wildlife throughout the American West. Through patience and observation, John Ritchey documents animal behavior in natural environments, capturing moments that reveal how animals communicate, hunt, protect their young, and respond to their surroundings. Long hours in remote areas require both awareness and respect for wildlife, while also providing opportunities to study movement, interaction, and instinct. John Ritchey is a professional wildlife photographer residing in Lincoln. He began pursuing photography as a full-time passion following his retirement in 2009 after serving 24 years as an Integrated Avionics Systems Mechanic for the Nebraska Air National Guard. From 2007-2008, he also served as a house photographer for the Qwest Center. View his gallery: https://api.flickr.com/people/ritcheyjj/. events.title: 'Remembering Modern Art' Curator Tour
events.description: Join Sheldon's chief curator and associate director for curatorial affairs, Magdalena Moskalewicz, for a special tour of "Remembering Modern Art." This exhibition explores the forces-museums, exhibitions, artists, and cultural diplomacy-that shaped the story of American modern art in the twentieth century. The guided tours offer insights into MoAA's collection as well as Sheldon's place within the history of modern art. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: "Grace Hartigan: The Gift of Attention" - with curator Jared Ledesma
events.description: Exhibition curator Jared Ledesma celebrates Grace Hartigan: The Gift of Attention, with a special welcome and poetry reading by JC Andrews. Drawing from his work organizing the exhibition, Ledesma will offer insight into Hartigan's practice and the creative exchange between her work and the influential New York poets who shaped her artistic world, including Frank O'Hara, Barbara Guest, and James Schuyler while forging one of the most distinctive voices in postwar American art.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Wildlife Photography by John Ritchey
events.description: Wildlife Photography is a collection of images captured across Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and Nebraska that highlights the beauty and behavior of wildlife throughout the American West. Through patience and observation, John Ritchey documents animal behavior in natural environments, capturing moments that reveal how animals communicate, hunt, protect their young, and respond to their surroundings. Long hours in remote areas require both awareness and respect for wildlife, while also providing opportunities to study movement, interaction, and instinct. John Ritchey is a professional wildlife photographer residing in Lincoln. He began pursuing photography as a full-time passion following his retirement in 2009 after serving 24 years as an Integrated Avionics Systems Mechanic for the Nebraska Air National Guard. From 2007-2008, he also served as a house photographer for the Qwest Center. View his gallery: https://api.flickr.com/people/ritcheyjj/. For purchase inquiries, he can be reached at (402) 610-5267 or jritc65610@yahoo.com. This exhibit is free and open to the public daily from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: 'Like a Moth to a Flame' opening reception
events.description: The opening reception for "Like a Moth to the Flame" will take place at the Great Plains Art Museum on Aug. 19, 6-8 p.m. with artist Jennifer Angus. Angus creates site-specific, immersive art installations that utilize dead and dried insect specimens to create environments that are often described as otherworldly, magical, and sometimes uncomfortable. Over time, Angus's work has evolved to consider issues related to the environment and the important role insects play within it. "Like a Moth to the Flame" explores the Great Plains region, an ecosystem home to the Sandhill crane migration, American bison, mountain lions, foxes, badgers, and countless other mammals. Less visible, though no less essential, are the nearly 30,000 insect species that inhabit this landscape, most living unseen beneath leaves, within soil, and among grasses. This exhibition invites visitors into that hidden world, asking them to imagine themselves insect-sized, dwarfed by the sculptural works around them. Within this immersive environment, the extraordinary adaptability of insects becomes visible, revealing how these small creatures sustain the intricate balance of an interconnected ecosystem. Angus is a professor of Design Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Described by "Art Daily" as "one of the top contemporary installation artists in the country," Angus has exhibited widely across the United States, being one of nine artists selected for the landmark exhibition "WONDER" at the Smithsonian American Art Museum's Renwick Gallery in 2015. This exhibition at the Great Plains Art Museum is presented in collaboration with CAREMI, the Community for Arthropod Research, Education, and Materials Innovation, a transdisciplinary initiative at UNL that brings together researchers, engineers, artists, educators, students, and community members to harness the diversity and resilience of arthropods as sources of knowledge, inspiration, and innovation. More at: https://caremi.unl.edu/ An opening reception will take place with an informal introduction by Angus. The reception follows Arthropodium 2026, CAREMI's annual symposium celebrating arthropod-inspired innovation across science, engineering, art and food. This exhibition is supported by the Nebraska Arts Council and the Nebraska Cultural Endowment.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Hands-On Soil Health Assessment: Field Sampling to Soil Health Scores
events.description: This is a practical, field-based soil health assessment training designed for agronomists, RCPP/RPPP contract holders, and Certified Crop Advisors. Participants will learn how to design efficient sampling plans using SSPOT concepts, collect soil samples following CEMA 216 and NRCS Technical Note 450, and conduct in-situ soil health evaluations in the field. We will then return to the shed to discuss observations, connect field data to lab-based indicators, and demonstrate how to use the SHAPE tool to generate soil health scores and inform management decisions. By the end of the day, attendees will be better equipped to integrate soil health testing into conservation planning and to support farmers in building and maintaining resilient, healthy soils. Registration is free thanks to sponsorship from the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment and the Nebraska Soybean Board and includes lunch and a soil health kit. Space is limited to 25 participants. Register by Aug. 20. Register here: https://unlcorexmuw.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a2BE9XiSESVztPw Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: NSPIRE: Supervisor's Playbook
events.description: Great supervisors develop habits and consistently carry out simple but effective tasks over time. This interactive workshop introduces the UNL Supervisor Playbook, a practical, research-backed toolkit that translates decades of workplace science into concrete, schedulable actions any supervisor can put directly on their calendar and start using this week. The Playbook is built on research: Gallup Q12, CliftonStrengths, Google's Project Oxygen and Project Aristotle, McKinsey's Organizational Health Index, and Great Place to Work studies. The same core supervisor behaviors show up across all of them, and this session is about how to build those behaviors into a realistic weekly and monthly rhythm. Every participant will receive a take-home Supervisor Playbook handout organized by practice category, including recognition, individual connection, feedback, growth and development, trust and autonomy, strategic alignment, and team culture. Each practice includes the recommended frequency and step-by-step guidance on how to actually do it. This session is designed for current supervisors at every experience level, and for aspiring leaders who want to be intentional about developing their skills before they need them. Click here to register: https://nebraska.bridgeapp.com/learner/training/b9eb476c/enrollPractical Habits for Great People LeadersStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Wildlife Photography by John Ritchey
events.description: Wildlife Photography is a collection of images captured across Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and Nebraska that highlights the beauty and behavior of wildlife throughout the American West. Through patience and observation, John Ritchey documents animal behavior in natural environments, capturing moments that reveal how animals communicate, hunt, protect their young, and respond to their surroundings. Long hours in remote areas require both awareness and respect for wildlife, while also providing opportunities to study movement, interaction, and instinct. John Ritchey is a professional wildlife photographer residing in Lincoln. He began pursuing photography as a full-time passion following his retirement in 2009 after serving 24 years as an Integrated Avionics Systems Mechanic for the Nebraska Air National Guard. From 2007-2008, he also served as a house photographer for the Qwest Center. View his gallery: https://api.flickr.com/people/ritcheyjj/. For purchase inquiries, he can be reached at (402) 610-5267 or jritc65610@yahoo.com. This exhibit is free and open to the public daily from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Farm Disaster Tax Rules: Deferrals, Casualty Losses, Recovery Payments and Tax Reporting
events.description: The Nebraska Tax Institute, part of the College of Business, is offering a new webinar Thursday, Aug. 27, to help tax professionals navigate federal tax rules affecting agricultural producers following wildfires, drought, floods, storms and other disasters. Agricultural disaster tax rules aren't something you use every day. But when your clients need them, knowing which rules apply and how to apply them can make a lasting difference for their operation. Join agricultural tax and farm management experts Tina Barrett, EA, and Mark Dikeman, EA, for a practical, four-hour webinar covering the federal tax rules that apply when agricultural producers are affected by wildfire, drought, floods, storms and other casualty or disaster events. You'll learn how to move from "something bad happened" to a clear tax plan for your clients by identifying which rules apply, gathering the right information, evaluating deferral options and understanding how today's decisions can affect basis, depreciation, future gains and financial recovery.Status: CONFIRMED | -

events.location: Mary Riepma Ross Media Arts Center-Van Brunt Visitors Center Room:Ross Theaters (123 & 124)
events.description: Showing at The Ross August 28-September 3. Visit theross.org for tickets, showtimes, and more information. The great Willem Dafoe lends his delicate gravitas to the role of Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer (Edmund Donovan) appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention-and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group's "tragic heroine" (a sinuous, Kurt Weill-crooning Greta Lee)-Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. This thoughtful, witty second feature from Kent Jones (DIANE), working from a sly and hugely entertaining script by Oscar nominated screenwriter Samy Burch (MAY DECEMBER, is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.Ross MovieStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Wildlife Photography by John Ritchey
events.description: Wildlife Photography is a collection of images captured across Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and Nebraska that highlights the beauty and behavior of wildlife throughout the American West. Through patience and observation, John Ritchey documents animal behavior in natural environments, capturing moments that reveal how animals communicate, hunt, protect their young, and respond to their surroundings. Long hours in remote areas require both awareness and respect for wildlife, while also providing opportunities to study movement, interaction, and instinct. John Ritchey is a professional wildlife photographer residing in Lincoln. He began pursuing photography as a full-time passion following his retirement in 2009 after serving 24 years as an Integrated Avionics Systems Mechanic for the Nebraska Air National Guard. From 2007-2008, he also served as a house photographer for the Qwest Center. View his gallery: https://api.flickr.com/people/ritcheyjj/. For purchase inquiries, he can be reached at (402) 610-5267 or jritc65610@yahoo.com. This exhibit is free and open to the public daily from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: What's in a Database?
events.description: This workshop will provide participants with essential skills for getting started with research. Come with a topic in mind to practice what you learn as we go! There will be a 1-hour presentation and an optional half-hour afterward for practice and questions for the librarians. The first half of the session will cover library resources and the basics of identifying and searching in library databases. You will learn about Boolean operators and identifying key words for database searching. The second half of the session will cover more advanced techniques for building efficient and thorough search strategies for graduate level and upper-undergraduate level literature reviews, including making your search more comprehensive and less biased. It will also cover techniques for testing your search strategies for both precision and sensitivity. There will be activities to practice skills and time at the end to run practice searches for your own research. So be sure to bring a topic for a paper you may be working on for a class or publication and get a strong start to your semester. Register at https://unl.libcal.com/calendar/workshops/databasesDeveloping skills for searching the academic literatureStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Department of Biochemistry and Redox Biology Center Seminar Series
events.description: Dr. Dave Pagliarini is an HHMI and BJC Investigator and the Hugo F. and Ina C. Urbauer Professor at Washington University School of Medicine (WashU Med). At WashU Med, Dave leads an interdisciplinary team of scientists focusing on a range of leading-edge challenges in mitochondrial biochemistry and metabolism. In particular, his lab blends large-scale systems approaches with mechanistic biochemistry to define the molecular underpinnings of mitochondria dysfunction in human disease. Dave has received a number of honors for his work, including a Searle Scholar Award, the Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE), the Young Investigator award from the Protein Society, the Earl and Thressa Stadtman Young Scholar Award from the ASBMB, and in was elected as a fellow in the 2025 class of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)."Wiring mitochondria: The biochemistry and biosynthesis of coenzyme Q"Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Peace Corps Prep Application Deadline
events.description: Integrating UNL coursework, hands-on experience, and professional development, Nebraska’s Peace Corps Prep program prepares undergraduates for volunteer service globally, potentially with the Peace Corps, by building the following four core competencies: 1) Sector-specific skills (in Education, Health, Environment, Agriculture, Youth in Development, or Community Economic Development) 2) Foreign language proficiency 3) Intercultural competence 4) Professional savvy and leadership Upon completion of the program, you will receive a certificate from the Peace Corps, a federal agency. Completing the PC Prep program gives you a competitive edge when applying for Peace Corps service, but does not guarantee acceptance as a Peace Corps Volunteer. Special features of the PC Prep program at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln include: *Eligibility for competitive scholarship to study or intern abroad in a country where Peace Corps volunteers have served. *Tailored education abroad advising and Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI) assessment upon acceptance and completion. *Social/networking events, group volunteer experiences, and announcements about related campus and community events. *Opportunities to engage with Returned Peace Corps Volunteers in the community through events and mentorship. *Culminating zero-credit course listed on the transcript, recognition in campus media outlets, and a cord to wear at graduation. events.title: What's in a Database?
events.description: This workshop will provide participants with essential skills for getting started with research. Come with a topic in mind to practice what you learn as we go! There will be a 1-hour presentation and an optional half-hour afterward for practice and questions for the librarians. The first half of the session will cover library resources and the basics of identifying and searching in library databases. You will learn about Boolean operators and identifying key words for database searching. The second half of the session will cover more advanced techniques for building efficient and thorough search strategies for graduate level and upper-undergraduate level literature reviews, including making your search more comprehensive and less biased. It will also cover techniques for testing your search strategies for both precision and sensitivity. There will be activities to practice skills and time at the end to run practice searches for your own research. So be sure to bring a topic for a paper you may be working on for a class or publication and get a strong start to your semester. Register at https://unl.libcal.com/calendar/workshops/databasesDINSDeveloping skills for searching the academic literatureStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Van Jensen
events.description: UNL and Daily Nebraskan alum Van Jensen will read from his novel GODFALL, a blend of sci-fi and murder mystery. GODFALL was the subject of a Hollywood bidding war, with the rights going to Imagine Entertainment. Academy Award-winner Ron Howard will direct the TV series. About GODFALL: When a massive asteroid hurtles toward Earth, humanity braces for annihilation-but the end doesn't come. In fact, it isn't an asteroid but a three-mile-tall alien that drops down, seemingly dead, outside Little Springs, Nebraska. Dubbed "the giant," its arrival transforms the red-state farm town into a top-secret government research site and major metropolitan area, flooded with soldiers, scientists, bureaucrats, spies, criminals, conspiracy theorists-and a murderer. About the author: Van Jensen was born and raised in the farm country of Western Nebraska where he wrote and drew stories as soon as he could hold a pencil. He became a newspaper crime reporter, then a magazine editor, and eventually an author of comic books and graphic novels. He has written some of the world's biggest characters, including James Bond and The Flash, Superman, Wonder Woman and the Green Lantern Corps for DC Comics. He also has co-created acclaimed series including TWO DEAD from Simon & Schuster/Gallery 13 (with National Book Award-winning artist Nate Powell), CRYPTOCRACY from Dark Horse (with Pete Woods), and PINOCCHIO, VAMPIRE SLAYER from Top Shelf/IDW (with Dusty Higgins).Reading/DiscussionStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: 2026 Krivosha Lecture
events.description: 2026 Krivosha Lecture presents Zalman Rothschild, Assistant Professor of Law and the Horn Family Distinguished Research Scholar in Law and Religion at the Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law. His lecture will put Jewish law in conversation with the ongoing debate over how the Free Exercise Clause of the First Amendment should be construed. A bedrock assumption in free exercise jurisprudence is that religion's mandates are absolute. But religious norms do not always operate that way. Jewish law, for example, is often nonbinary and spectrum-based. It is an elaborate system of flexible standards and sliding-scale rules that enables religious practitioners to live under secular rule. Jewish law, then, allows us to reexamine a common assumption underlying free exercise jurisprudence. It also raises the question whether, in some instances at least, religious freedom itself incentivizes the reshaping of religion as unyielding where previously it was understood to be flexible.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Department of Biochemistry and Redox Biology Center Seminar Series
events.description: Dr. Xingshui Sun : The long-term goal of my laboratory is to define how vascular endothelial dysfunction drives cardiometabolic conditions, translating these insights into actionable therapies. events.title: Seminar Series: Larissa Carneiro
events.description: Larissa Carneiro, PhD, will present "Substance Use Disorder: The Healing Promises of Ayahuasca" at the RDAR Center's September Seminar Series. This virtual event is free and open to the public. Register here to receive the Zoom link: https://unl.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_wNdfb_U-S8mR5F6RQhqtyQ - More Event Info - Since the 1990s, the healing promises of ayahuasca have drawn increasing attention from both Brazilian and international scientific communities. Recent clinical studies have explored ayahuasca's possible therapeutic effects for conditions such as depression, anxiety, and substance use disorder. This growing interest echoes what ayahuasca-using religions have affirmed for decades: the brew has curative powers. In this seminar, Dr. Carneiro will discuss the religious context in which these healing claims take shape, focusing specifically on the Church of Santo Daime, where ayahuasca functions simultaneously as sacrament and medicine. Dr. Carneiro is a Lecturing Fellow in the Department of Religious Studies at Duke University. Her research examines the intersections of religion, magic, and science, with a particular emphasis on healing practices involving sacred plants. Her current ethnographic project, "Ayahuasca in Brazil: Where Religion Meets Science", investigates how religious rituals, communal settings, and belief systems shape healing experiences that incorporate ayahuasca. Rural Drug Addiction Research CenterStatus: CONFIRMED | -

events.title: Elsewhere / The Prairie Was Ours: Artist Talk by Elizabeth Burden
events.description: Through the work of three artists-Elizabeth Burden, Willa Ahlschwede, and Marci Sue Black-the exhibition "Elsewhere / The Prairie Was Ours" positions the prairie as a site where stories are entangled across generations, geographies, and historical conditions. Situated within ongoing public debates about land, settlement, identity, and United States history, "Elsewhere" considers how the prairie functions as both material landscape and ideological terrain shaped by settler colonialism, migration, and inherited narratives of place, which remain in rhizomatic relation. In this artist talk, Burden will engage audiences in thinking about the layered histories of the landscapes we inherit and how art can create space to unearth and unsettle, remember, and reimagine them. Burden is the Great Plains Art Museum's 2026 Elizabeth Rubendall Artist in Residence. "Elsewhere / The Prairie Was Ours" is on view at the Great Plains Art Museum Aug. 25 to Dec. 19, 2026. Burden is an artist who engages in artistic archivy: the blending multidisciplinary studio work with social practice to reflect on the past/present/future. She is intrigued by the pull of archives, the construction of histories, ephemeral inheritances, the role of memory and narrative, and the ways we make sense of it all. She uses a variety of media to create space for critical thinking, critical feeling, and critical reflection that may lead to a re-imagining of possibilities. She was born and raised in Lincoln; as the great-granddaughter of the first Black homesteaders in Nebraska (Henry and Mary Burden), she is a third-generation Nebraskan, now living in the Southwest. Photo by Deanna DentArtist in ResidenceStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Native American Film Series
events.location: Mary Riepma Ross Media Arts Center-Van Brunt Visitors Center Room:Ross Theater (123)
events.description: Now in it's third year, the Native American Film Series at The Ross features free monthly screenings showcasing Native American films and television programs from the Vision Maker Media public broadcasting archives. Presented by The Ross Media Arts Center, Vision Maker Media, and Friends of The Ross. Unless otherwise noted, screenings in this series will take place on the second Monday of each month and are admission free and open to the public. Tickets available at the Ross box office (online ticketing not available for free screenings). Showing in June: AANIKOOBIJIGAN [ANCESTOR / GREAT-GRANDPARENT / GREAT-GRANDCHILD] // In the sterile archives of museums our ancestor's remains struggle to find their way home. The film follows the eleven indigenous repatriation specialists that make up MACPRA (Michigan Anishinaabek Cultural Preservation & Repatriation Alliance). Through an essayistic approach the film takes a critical look at the reasoning that justified unearthing and collecting them in the first place, and presents vrit portraits of the courageous individuals doing the hard and emotionally draining work of fighting for their return. The June 8 screening will be followed by a discussion with Zack Khalil (Director/Producer/Cinematographer), Jacque Clark (Producer/Additional Cinematographer/Sound Recordist), and Samuli Haavisto (Cinematographer). Moderated by Shirley Sneve (ICT Newscast Senior Producer).Ross EventStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Department of Biochemistry and Redox Biology Center Seminar Series
events.description: Thrombosis is a key component of cardiovascular diseases and is the underlying cause of one in four deaths worldwide. I study the scavenger clearance receptor, stabilin-2, whose deficiency is associated with an increased risk of venous thrombosis. I identified novel ligands for this receptor including proteins with roles in coagulation and inflammation, increased levels of which increase thrombosis risk. I aim to identify the molecular mechanisms governing stabilin-2's interactions with its ligands and the role of clearance receptors in thrombosis development. "Stabilin-2 at the Interface of Coagulation Protein Turnover and Thrombosis"Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Great Plains Talk: Caleb Gayle
events.description: Caleb Gayle will give a talk about his book, "Black Moses: A Saga of Ambition and the Fight for a Black State" (2025, Penguin Random House), as the winner of the 2026 Stubbendieck Great Plains Distinguished Book Prize. In "Black Moses," also longlisted for the National Book Award, Gayle recounts the extraordinary tale of Edward McCabe, a Black man who championed idea to create a state within the U.S. governed by and for Black people - and the racism, politics and greed that thwarted him. As the sweeping changes brought by the Civil War and Reconstruction began to wither, anger at the opportunities available to newly freed Black people rose and both Blacks and whites searched for new places to settle. That was when McCabe, a Black businessman and a rising political star in the American West, set in motion his plans to found a state. His chosen site: Oklahoma, a place that the U.S. government had deeded to Indigenous people in the 1830s when it forced thousands of them to leave their homes under Indian Removal. "Winning the Stubbendieck is both surprising but affirming of my goal to help readers see this part of the country for all of its diversity and rich complexity," Gayle said. Gayle is an award-winning journalist author "We Refuse to Forget: A True Story of Black Creeks, American Identity, and Power." A professor at Northeastern University, he is a contributing writer at"The New York Times Magazine." Gayle will be awarded the book prize as part of this event. This talk is part of the Paul A. Olson Great Plains Seminar Series. Each year the Center for Great Plains Studies presents the Stubbendieck Great Plains Distinguished Book Prize for the previous year's best book on the Great Plains. The prize carries a cash award of $10,000, generously supported by Jim and Cheryl Stubbendieck. Only first edition, full-length, nonfiction books copyrighted in 2025 were evaluated for this year's award, which is chosen by an independent committee.BOOK PRIZE WINNERStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Constitution Day 2026
events.description: The University of Nebraska-Lincoln will commemorate Constitution Day with a full day of public programming focused on the U.S. Constitution and contemporary constitutional issues. Constitution Day is a federal day of observance set aside to recognize the signing of the U.S. Constitution on September 17, 1787, and to encourage constitutional literacy and civic engagement. The event will feature live oral arguments by the Nebraska Court of Appeals, providing students and members of the public with an opportunity to observe the appellate process in action. Court sessions are scheduled for 9:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. The day will conclude with a panel discussion by legal scholars: "Can the First Amendment Adapt to Artificial Intelligence?" This panel will explore whether the First Amendment's existing principles adequately address AI-generated expression, or if the rise of artificial intelligence requires us to rethink fundamental assumptions about speech, authorship, and constitutional protections. The event is free and open to the public. Constitution Day oral arguments are sponsored by the Department of Political Science, Nebraska Bar Foundation, and Nebraska Court of Appeals. Constitution Day panel is sponsored by the Department of Political Science and the UNL AI Institute.Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Zanna Gilbert Lecture
events.description: Zanna Gilbert, senior research specialist at the Getty Research Institute in Los Angeles, presents on her exhibition "How to Be a Guerrilla Girl" and explores how archival and curatorial research illuminates the histories of feminist, conceptual and activist art practices. About Dr. Zanna Gilbert Dr. Zanna Gilbertis a senior research specialist at the Getty Research Institute. Her research focuses on transnational conceptual art, feminisms, and the international mail art network, with a particular focus on Latin America. She received an AHRC Collaborative Doctoral Award to complete her PhD at the School of Philosophy and Art History at the University of Essex and Tate Research, where she researched and wrote about the museum's collections of Latin American art. She was previously an Andrew W. Mellon postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Drawings and Prints at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York, where she led research on Latin America and was founding co-editor of the online publicationpost: notes on modern and contemporary art around the globe. At the Getty, she is co-lead of the Latin American and Latinx Art History Initiative (LALAI) and several research projects. She is co-curator of the exhibitionTransgresoras: Mail Art and Messages, 1960s-2020s(California Museum of Photography, UCR ARTS, 2025-26), as well asHow to Be a Guerrilla Girl(Getty Research Institute, 2025-26). She is co-editor of the publicationEd Ruscha's Streets of Los Angeles: Artist, Image, Archive, City(2025) and is currently working on an exhibition and publication titledPioneers of a New Image: Women Artists and Xerography, forthcoming in 2027-28. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Beyond ChatGPT
events.description: Since the introduction of ChatGPT 3.5 in late 2022, we seem to have entered a world surrounded by Large Language Models (LLMs), often without a clear understanding of how these models work. While the internal workings of LLMs remain largely a black box, this does not mean we should treat LLMs themselves as black boxes hidden behind a chat interface. This workshop aims to make LLMs more visible and tangible through hands-on interaction with open-source models available on Hugging Face using Google Colab. Participants will learn fundamental concepts of LLMs through practical exercises that will hopefully provide a better understanding of both their strengths and limitations when interacting with these models in the future. No prior coding experience is required. However, a Google account is necessary to access Google Colab, so please create one before the workshop if needed.Hands-On Interaction with Open-Source Large Language Models (LLMs) in Google ColabStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Kurt Andersen
events.description: Originally from Omaha, Kurt Andersen has been documenting arts, culture, and politics in New York City for decades. In the spring 2026 issue of Prairie Schooner, Andersen wrote about Edward Hopper's ROOM IN NEW YORK, the iconic NYC painting by Edward Hopper in the Sheldon's permanent collection. He will discuss the essay, and introduce his latest novel, THE BREAKUP, which is set in 2045, following the collapse of a marriage on a road trip through a strange, uncertain new American landscape, transformed by both terrorist uprising and technology. Kurt Andersen is the bestselling author of EVIL GENIUSES, FANTASYLAND and the novels TRUE BELIEVERS, HEYDAY and TURN OF THE CENTURY, among other books. He contributes to The New York Times and was host and co-creator of Studio 360, the Peabody Award-winning public radio show and podcast. He also writes for television, film, and the stage. Andersen co-founded Spy magazine, served as editor in chief of New York, and was a cultural columnist and design critic for Time, New York and The New Yorker. events.title: Kazim Ali
events.description: Kazim Ali reads from THE MAN IN 119, his new collection of poetry. The book explores loss and absence alongside the human body and the natural world. Here, the tongue becomes a collaboration between human and glacial current-the self, a "tectonic topography of god." Grappling with questions of mortality in the wake of his mother's passing, Ali asks where we go when we leave this world: "earth or sky or memory only." With musicality, these poems build a space for contemplation, offering vignettes of various individuals, memories, and geographies. We learn that in migration, the body moves, reproduces itself through the experience of losing and living still. Kazim Ali was born in the United Kingdom and has lived transnationally in the United States, Canada, India, France, and the Middle East. His books encompass multiple genres, including several volumes of poetry, novels, and translations. He is currently a Professor of Literature at the University of California, San Diego. Among his recent books are a volume of three long poems entitled THE VOICE OF SHEILA CHANDRA and a memoir of his Canadian childhood, NORTHERN LIGHT: POWER, LAND, AND THE MEMORY OF WATER. Status: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Nebraska Lecture featuring Jay Storz
events.description: The Nebraska Lecture, scheduled for October 6, "Life Ascending: Extreme Animals and Exploration in the High Andes," will feature Jay F. Storz, Willa Cather Professor in the School of Biological Sciences. What are the environmental limits of animal life? Jay Storz and his South American collaborators are addressing this question by conducting extreme high-elevation surveys of Andean animals. The fieldwork involves a combination of mountain climbing and zoological surveys in extremely remote regions of the Central Andes that are unexplored by biologists. These surveys have yielded new world records for multiple species of small mammals (mostly mice!) living on or near the summits of more than 22,000 volcanoes. Such elevations were previously thought to be completely uninhabitable. Ongoing genomic and physiological experiments are revealing the adaptive mechanisms that enable the high-elevation mice to survive in such hostile conditions. Storz's talk will also cover indigenous Andean cultures, from the time of the Incan Empire to the present, and their relationship to sacred Andean peaks. Storz's lecture will be provided in-person at the Nebraska Union, Swanson Auditorium, at 3:30 p.m., followed by a live moderated Q&A. Reception in Regency Suite to follow lecture. The Nebraska Lectures: Chancellor's Distinguished Lecture Series features presentations by distinguished university faculty. In collaboration with the Office of Research and Innovation, the Research Council established this lecture series in 2003. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.description: Now in it's third year, the Native American Film Series at The Ross features free monthly screenings showcasing Native American films and television programs from the Vision Maker Media public broadcasting archives. Showing in June: AANIKOOBIJIGAN [ANCESTOR / GREAT-GRANDPARENT / GREAT-GRANDCHILD] // In the sterile archives of museums our ancestor's remains struggle to find their way home. The film follows the eleven indigenous repatriation specialists that make up MACPRA (Michigan Anishinaabek Cultural Preservation & Repatriation Alliance). events.title: Leading Through Resistance: How to Help Your Team Get Unstuck
events.description: Most supervisors have a natural "fixing reflex"-when an employee struggles or resists a new change, we want to jump in and give them the answer. But telling people what to do often backfires, making them more defensive and less likely to actually change. This workshop is built for leaders who deal with the tough stuff: employees who are stuck, hesitant, or just plain unwilling to move forward. While standard coaching works for people who are already motivated, this session gives you the tools to handle the hard conversations where motivation is missing. You will learn how to stop being the "expert" who does all the work and start being the leader who helps staff find their own reasons to improve. By the end of this session, you'll know how to lower workplace tension, stop the "push-and-pull" of managing difficult transitions, and help your team take real pride in their own progress. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Health Equity Grand Rounds: Ciera Kirkpatrick
events.description: Join us for our October Grand Rounds to hear from Ciera Kirkpatrick, PhD, about "Scrolling Through Motherhood: How Social Media Shapes Maternal Mental Health." The event is FREE and open to the public. Register for the Zoom link: https://unl.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_MefhgDCBSey4eFd_f4h6sg#/registration Today's mothers are navigating motherhood in a world saturated with social media. From carefully curated parenting posts on Instagram to postpartum "bounce back" fitspiration videos on TikTok, social media is exacerbating the culture of comparison and shaping maternal mental health in ways we are only beginning to understand. In this talk, Dr. Kirkpatrick will discuss findings from a series of experiments examining how idealized social media content influences mothers' anxiety, shame, body image, and confidence in their parenting abilities. She will also discuss a promising strategy for reducing the harms of social media comparisons. This talk will bring attention to social media's effects on mental health and what we can do about it. Dr. Kirkpatrick is an Assistant Professor of Advertising and Public Relations at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln College of Journalism and Mass Communications. Her research uses a social scientific experimental approach to investigate how messaging in the media (e.g., advertising, news, social media content) affects individuals' mental and physical health and how strategic communicators can effectively design messages to improve individuals' health outcomes. Learn more about Dr. Kirkpatrick: https://journalism.unl.edu/person/ciera-kirkpatrick/ Minority Health Disparities Initiative Status: CONFIRMED | -

events.title: Filles du Roi (The King's Daughters): Founding Mothers of Canada
events.description: From 1663-1673, nearly 800 women traveled from their homes in France to marry men in Canada as part of a program commonly called The King's Daughters. These marriageable women were recruited, received financial support and other benefits from the King/government. It is calculated that these women are ancestors of 2/3rds of today's Canadian population and millions of Americans of French-Canadian descent. Join Joan Barnes, communications librarian, on October 20 for a fascinating look at the program and a few of the 30+ women in her personal family tree that are considered the founding mothers of Canada. Join the Genealogy over Lunch session on October 20 from 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. on Zoom. Registration required. Genealogy Over LunchStatus: CONFIRMED | -

events.title: Living Up to Openness
events.description: As researchers face growing pressure to demonstrate the impact of their work amid the increasing metrification of research assessment, developing metrics literacy is essential not only as a form of self-protection but also as a means of empower researchers to advocate for the responsible use of metrics within and beyond their institutions. This workshop introduces a practical workflow for tracking and demonstrating research impact that is grounded in open science principles and supported by open scholarly infrastructure, including ORCID, Zotero, OpenAlex, and R. The first part of the workshop highlights common pitfalls of widely used metrics, such as the h-index and Journal Impact Factor (JIF), and explores alternative, more inclusive indicators for evaluating research impact. The second part consists of a hands-on session using R to retrieve bibliographic records via the OpenAlex API and to generate descriptive statistics and visualization of research impact. No prior programming experience is required. However, participants should bring their own laptops and are strongly encouraged to install R and RStudio before attending. For those who encounter technical difficulties, we have partnered with Holland Computing Center (HCC) to provide demo accounts for accessing RStudio through HCC OnDemand. Participants are also encouraged to register for an ORCID iD and to maintain their records of publications and creative works in Zotero. A sample dataset will be provided for anyone who does not bring their own data.A Practical Workflow for Tracking and Demonstrating Research ImpactStatus: CONFIRMED | - |

events.description: The Herr lab uses biophysical and structural approaches to illuminate how key staphylococcal proteins mediate host adhesion and biofilm formation. They showed that the surface protein Aap self-assembles in the presence of zinc to form twisted, rope-like structures between staphylococcal cells in a nascent biofilm. This work led to the development of an antibacterial platform that was licensed and taken to clinical trials. Recent work has focused on the role of Aap in adhesion to healthy skin and protein-DNA interactions leading to biomolecular condensate formation in the biofilm matrix. "The biophysics of bacterial biofilms: mechanisms of staphylococcal intercellular adhesion"Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Hope Wabuke
events.description: UNL English professor Hope Wabuke reads from her new book, BLOOD ON THE LEAVES, a searing and lyrical poetry collection that explores the intimate, haunted relationship between Blackness and the natural world. At once a site of refuge and rupture, nature emerges as both witness to generational trauma and a space of beauty, survival, and fierce possibility. Hewn from historical record and personal experience, these poems unearth the brutal legacy of slavery and the enduring persistence of systemic racism, tracing how violence echoes through land, body, and bloodline. Wabuke weaves history, science, and the environment into the personal-examining gender, motherhood, identity, and the Black body as sites of resistance and remembrance. BLOOD ON THE LEAVES, a collection of poetryStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Prepare Now for Your Personal Digital Dark Age
events.description: All digital files are vulnerable to decay and loss. Sometimes a hard drive fails or a file becomes corrupted. But we can also lose files due to bad data management habits, obsolete technology, or, paradoxically, because we have too many copies and too many storage options. It is easy to overlook the digital photos, documents, and other files we create in daily life, in our personal research, and in our citizen science and historian scholarship. This workshop helps participants identify their most valuable computer files and create a plan for backup, self-curation, and preservation. Side effects may include improved ability to find and share files, and more restful sleep at night. Research Data Librarian Scout Calvert hosts this workshop in recognition of World Digital Preservation Day.Status: CONFIRMED | -

events.title: Native American Film Series
events.location: Mary Riepma Ross Media Arts Center-Van Brunt Visitors Center Room:Ross Theater (123)
events.description: Now in it's third year, the Native American Film Series at The Ross features free monthly screenings showcasing Native American films and television programs from the Vision Maker Media public broadcasting archives. Presented by The Ross Media Arts Center, Vision Maker Media, and Friends of The Ross. Unless otherwise noted, screenings in this series will take place on the second Monday of each month and are admission free and open to the public. Tickets available at the Ross box office (online ticketing not available for free screenings). Showing in June: AANIKOOBIJIGAN [ANCESTOR / GREAT-GRANDPARENT / GREAT-GRANDCHILD] // In the sterile archives of museums our ancestor's remains struggle to find their way home. The film follows the eleven indigenous repatriation specialists that make up MACPRA (Michigan Anishinaabek Cultural Preservation & Repatriation Alliance). Through an essayistic approach the film takes a critical look at the reasoning that justified unearthing and collecting them in the first place, and presents vrit portraits of the courageous individuals doing the hard and emotionally draining work of fighting for their return. The June 8 screening will be followed by a discussion with Zack Khalil (Director/Producer/Cinematographer), Jacque Clark (Producer/Additional Cinematographer/Sound Recordist), and Samuli Haavisto (Cinematographer). Moderated by Shirley Sneve (ICT Newscast Senior Producer).Ross EventStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Michael Lowenthal & Scott Heim
events.description: Michael Lowenthal will discuss his new book, PLACE ENVY: ESSAYS IN SEARCH OF ORIENTATION, and Scott Heim will discuss the reissue of his classic novel of gay literature, MYSTERIOUS SKIN. Growing up in places where his family had no past, and met mostly by silence from his Holocaust-refugee grandparents, Michael Lowenthal longed to be from somewhere. Then he realized he was gay and felt displaced from his own displaced family. PLACE ENVY-his first book of essays after five acclaimed books of fiction-chronicles his quest for orientation in the world: as an agnostic Jew, as a queer traveler and lover, and as a writer who can tell or twist the truth. Scott Heim's MYSTERIOUS SKIN is as timely and compelling as when it was first published more than three decades ago; this propulsive novel about abuse and its after-effects in the lives of two teenage boys is an honest and searing exploration of memory, survival, friendship, and the power of truth. The novel was adapted into film by Gregg Araki and released in 2004.Reading/discussionStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Department of Biochemistry and Redox Biology Center Seminar Series
events.description: Copper is an essential trace element for growth and development because copper acts as an indispensable cofactor for an array of enzymes, and mutations of genes involved in copper transport result in severe, even lethal, neurodegenerative diseases. Since copper is potentially toxic, appropriate copper levels are tightly regulated by a sophisticated network of copper transporters, chaperones and acceptors, which orchestrate the uptake, distribution, storage and release of this essential metal. The principal copper transporters include the plasma-membrane high-affinity copper importer, CTR1, and the copper-exporting ATPases ATP7A and ATP7B, in which mutations cause Menkes and Wilson's diseases, respectively. Here we discuss our recent progress in elucidating the molecular mechanisms of copper transport in these transporters and aim to develop a comprehensive molecular understanding of cellular copper transport, thus establishing a foundation for designing novel therapeutics for the treatment of copper metabolism diseases.Molecular Mechanisms of Copper Transport"Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Department of Biochemistry and Redox Biology Center Seminar Series
events.description: Our Microbial Ecophysiology Laboratory at UConn studies the biology of methanogenic archaea (methanogens) and their role in human and ecosystem health. In this talk, I will present our progress in characterizing the mechanisms by which methanogens respond to stress induced by sunlight, oxygen, and nutrient availability. Using model strains of methanogens found in anaerobic sediments and the human gut, we investigate how redox-related stress influences cellular homeostasis, survival, and phenotypic plasticity. Our results show that these stress conditions induce changes in the biochemistry of metabolic pathways and in cell morphology, while simultaneously activating response and repair mechanisms."Physiological responses of methanogenic archaea to redox stress" - Geo Santiago-Martnez, Ph.D. Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.title: Native American Film Series
events.location: Mary Riepma Ross Media Arts Center-Van Brunt Visitors Center Room:Ross Theater (123)
events.description: Now in it's third year, the Native American Film Series at The Ross features free monthly screenings showcasing Native American films and television programs from the Vision Maker Media public broadcasting archives. Presented by The Ross Media Arts Center, Vision Maker Media, and Friends of The Ross. Unless otherwise noted, screenings in this series will take place on the second Monday of each month and are admission free and open to the public. Tickets available at the Ross box office (online ticketing not available for free screenings). Showing in June: AANIKOOBIJIGAN [ANCESTOR / GREAT-GRANDPARENT / GREAT-GRANDCHILD] // In the sterile archives of museums our ancestor's remains struggle to find their way home. The film follows the eleven indigenous repatriation specialists that make up MACPRA (Michigan Anishinaabek Cultural Preservation & Repatriation Alliance). Through an essayistic approach the film takes a critical look at the reasoning that justified unearthing and collecting them in the first place, and presents vrit portraits of the courageous individuals doing the hard and emotionally draining work of fighting for their return. The June 8 screening will be followed by a discussion with Zack Khalil (Director/Producer/Cinematographer), Jacque Clark (Producer/Additional Cinematographer/Sound Recordist), and Samuli Haavisto (Cinematographer). Moderated by Shirley Sneve (ICT Newscast Senior Producer).Ross EventStatus: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Mamma Mia!
events.location: Lied Center for Performing Arts Room:Lied Center Main Stage
events.description: A mother. A daughter. 3 possible dads. And a trip down the aisleyou'll never forget! Set on a Greek island paradise where the sun always shines, a tale of love, friendship, and identity is beautifully told through the timeless hits of ABBA. On the eve of her wedding, a daughter's quest to discover the father she's never known brings three men from her mother's past back to the island they last visited decades ago. For over 25 years, people all around the world have fallen in love with the characters, the story, and the music that make MAMMA MIA! the ultimate feel-good show.Status: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Peace Corps Prep Application Deadline
events.description: Integrating UNL coursework, hands-on experience, and professional development, Nebraska’s Peace Corps Prep program prepares undergraduates for volunteer service globally, potentially with the Peace Corps, by building the following four core competencies: 1) Sector-specific skills (in Education, Health, Environment, Agriculture, Youth in Development, or Community Economic Development) 2) Foreign language proficiency 3) Intercultural competence 4) Professional savvy and leadership Upon completion of the program, you will receive a certificate from the Peace Corps, a federal agency. Completing the PC Prep program gives you a competitive edge when applying for Peace Corps service, but does not guarantee acceptance as a Peace Corps Volunteer. Special features of the PC Prep program at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln include: *Eligibility for competitive scholarship to study or intern abroad in a country where Peace Corps volunteers have served. *Tailored education abroad advising and Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI) assessment upon acceptance and completion. *Social/networking events, group volunteer experiences, and announcements about related campus and community events. *Opportunities to engage with Returned Peace Corps Volunteers in the community through events and mentorship. *Culminating zero-credit course listed on the transcript, recognition in campus media outlets, and a cord to wear at graduation. Learn more and start your application today!SpringStatus: CONFIRMED |

events.title: Popcorn Pop-Up
events.description: The best hour of the week! Every Thursday from 3 to 4 p.m. pop into The Crib for an afternoon social hour with 100s of other Huskers. It's free and every student, staff, and faculty is welcome. Snack on fresh-popped popcorn directly from the kettle. Join in the activity while learning about campus organizations and departments. Mingle with friends and new acquaintances. Remember: the Pop-Up is only 60 minutes. Arrive before 3 p.m. and you are there too early. Arrive after 4 p.m. and you missed it. ********** What to expect: Fun, fellowship, laughter, friends, and smiles. The activity is different each week. It might be trivia, or maybe a sport, a craft, or karaoke. You have to show up each week to find out. See the upcoming schedule at https://go.unl.edu/pop-up. There will always be fresh popcorn, including special mix-ins. ********** Earn a spot in the Golden Kernel Club. Discover the details: https://go.unl.edu/golden-kernel Status: CONFIRMED | - |

events.location: Lied Center for Performing Arts Room:Lied Center Main Stage
events.description: "Many wonders await audiences in this gorgeously imaginative Broadway musical." - The New York Times The critically acclaimed bestselling novel comes to "thrilling, dazzling" life (Time Out New York) in a unique, spectacle-filled new musical! After losing what matters most, a young man jumps a moving train unsure of where the road will take him and finds a new home with the remarkable crew of a traveling circus, and a life-and love-beyond his wildest dreams. Seen through the eyes of his older self, his adventure becomes a poignant reminder that if you choose the ride, life can begin again at any age. So, step right up to the "spellbinding entertainment" (Variety) at WATER FOR ELEPHANTS, "the best new musical on Broadway" (Theatermania). Recommended for ages 8 and up. Smoke, haze and gunshot sound effects are used in this production.Status: CONFIRMED | |

events.title: Daniil Trifonov
events.location: Lied Center for Performing Arts Room:Lied Center Main Stage
events.description: Praised as "the most astounding pianist of our age" by London's The Times, GRAMMY(R) Award-winning pianist Daniil Trifonov makes his Lied Center debut with a program showcasing extraordinary range. Handel's Suite No. 5 in E Major ("The Harmonious Blacksmith") opens the concert followed by Stravinsky's sole piano sonata and Schubert's beloved "Wanderer Fantasy," a powerful musical depiction of a stranger's search for meaning and happiness in a strange land. Trifonov's stylistic exploration continues on the program's second half featuring Brazilian, Argentine, and Dominican composers as well as his own original Tango! Combining consummate technique with rare sensitivity and depth, Trifonov's performances are a perpetual source of wonder to audiences and critics alike.Status: CONFIRMED | |
